definition: Congruent means in agreement — two things matching each other part for part.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word congruent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know congruent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The college's twin lecture halls are congruent down to the outlets — seat for seat, step for step — so a class can move from one to the other without renumbering a chair.
Compatible is weaker than congruent: compatible things merely get along without clashing, while congruent things answer each other part for part.
Identical goes further than congruent — congruent things match point for point yet remain two different things; identical means no difference is left at all.

For the centennial, the library displayed the new translation beside the hundred-year-old original, and readers kept remarking that the two books are congruent: chapter for chapter, joke for joke, even the page breaks fall in step — though the two texts do not share a single word.
Congruent names exactly that kind of match: part answering part, all the way through.
The books are not identical — they share no words at all — and they are more than merely compatible, more than two texts that happen not to contradict each other.
Congruent is the strong middle claim: two things that remain two things, built to one shape.
Congruent is the analyst's word for a fit you could verify item by item, and it usually travels with with: findings congruent with the record, conduct congruent with stated aims.
Its unit-mate consonant says two things share a spirit; congruent claims the stricter, part-for-part match.
Math class uses it for shapes that coincide exactly, and the same family gives congruous, congruity, and the far more common incongruous.

Before a pilot ever touches the real aircraft, she logs a hundred hours in the simulator, and the training only works because of one strict promise.
The simulator cabin must be congruent with the true cockpit -- every switch, lever, and gauge matching the real panel measurement for measurement.
A hand that reaches for the fuel cutoff in the dark has to find it in exactly the same place at exactly the same angle.
No one would call the two identical: the simulator is plastic and projection, weighs a fraction as much, and never leaves the ground.
What certification measures is the fit, piece answering piece, panel for panel.
